about: Accepted disagreements for scripts/check-highlighting-consistency.js. A rule matches a disagreement when every field matches: highlighter (textmate, tree-sitter or *), kind (mismatch or missing), rowan and other (coarse classes, other joined with + when several, or *), text (an optional regular expression the whole token text must match) and files (optional globs, relative to the repository root). Every rule carries a reason and a reference: a group of docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-textmate-vs-rowan-highlighting.md ('report group N'), a rowan defect filed as eu-oaz72.115, or a follow-up.

rules.reason: highlights.scm leaves plain name references uncaptured, in the editor's default face; rowan gives every reference a variable/function/property token
rowan marks declarations in a block passed as a call argument (merge({ a: 1 }), point-x{x: 3 y: 4}, io.return({ RESULT: :PASS })) as parameters
rowan marks the operands of operator and bracket declarations ((l +++ r):, (¬¬ x):, ⟦ xs ⟧:) as property declarations, not parameters
rowan marks block-destructuring parameters (f{x y}:, f({x y}):) as metadata: the leading soup of a block is read as block metadata
rowan gives s"..." type-data literals no semantic token
rowan marks every identifier in a metadata expression as metadata, values included (` { requires-io: true }, { monad: id })
rowan marks every identifier in a metadata expression as metadata, values included (` { requires-io: true }, { monad: id }); tree-sitter leaves those references uncaptured

rowan marks every identifier in a metadata expression as metadata; tree-sitter marks only the top-level keys of a metadata block as metadata, so keys of nested blocks ({ types: { Json: ... } }) are declarations
TextMate cannot recognise a unit's leading metadata block ({ import: ... }) or a block's leading metadata ({ :monad namespace: id }), so their keys are declarations
TextMate scopes the metadata operators // and //<< as keyword.operator.metadata; rowan marks them as operators
bracket-pair delimiters are anonymous regex tokens in the grammar, so highlights.scm can only capture the whole bracket_expr (@punctuation.special); rowan marks the delimiters as operators
rules.ref: follow-up: name the bracket delimiters in grammar.js

rules.reason: uncaptured names inside a bracket expression (⟦ xs ⟧:, ‹element(...) _value›) inherit the whole bracket_expr's @punctuation.special
rules.ref: follow-up: name the bracket delimiters in grammar.js

rules.reason: the tree-sitter grammar misparses these files without an ERROR node, so the corpus-parse check passes them: a symbol may have whitespace after its colon (a following declaration `β: y` becomes the soup `β :y` of the one before, and `{x: number}` in a string is an interpolation of `x :number`), a `{name:spec}` format spec is read as a symbol, and a plain string treats \" as an escape
rules.ref: follow-up: tree-sitter symbol, format-spec and plain-string lexing
